column1: # Sticker photo sources — paste the Pexels photo URL into the `url` column.
#   1. Click the search link, browse, pick a photo you like.
#   2. Copy the photo's page URL and paste it in the `url` column. Tab-separated.
#   3. Leave `url` blank for any you haven't chosen yet — the scripts skip those.
#        npm run fetch:stickers && npm run cut:stickers && npm run prepare:stickers
# WHERE TO LOOK — the search links below are only a starting point. If Pexels has
# nothing good (it skews to wide scenic shots, pairs, and herds), try:
#   Unsplash  https://unsplash.com/s/photos/<term>     free commercial, no attribution
#   Pixabay   https://pixabay.com/images/search/<term> free commercial, no attribution
#   Wikimedia https://commons.wikimedia.org            ⚠ licence varies, often CC BY-SA
# Columns 5 and 6 hold a direct image URL and a licence note. Only Pexels page URLs
# can be resolved automatically, so for any other host paste the direct image link
# into column 5 — or just give Claude the page URL and it will resolve it.
# WHAT MAKES A GOOD STICKER PHOTO
#   ✅ ONE subject, filling most of the frame, in focus
#   ✅ Background clearly separable (the subject gets cut out for the silhouette)
#   ✅ A real photograph — NOT an illustration, 3D render, figurine, or wooden toy
#   ❌ Subject small in a wide scene · multiple subjects · subject cropped at the edge
# --- 2a: letter-initial animals (19) — picture starts with the lesson's consonant ---
